description: Likely clashes: two entries that can both hold but sit badly together (a lost man who knows the stable's night arrangements). `a`, `b`: a fact id, or a possibility of a question `{q, pick}`; `why` in plain words; `available`: the paragraph from which it is shown; `from`: the reading (a thought) it comes from; `key`: the question at whose give-away it is listed ("a careful reader would have noticed"). In play a pair is shown only when one side is the player's own circle and the other is on the timeline (the user's ruling); strains the moves or certain contradictions already catch are not here (the poisoner who asks a witness to pass the poison; Simpson's admission; Mrs Straker's dress).

strains.why: A man who has lost his way would not know the stable's night arrangements.
The stranger came with his paper ready made: he could not have known the supper would be a dish strong enough to hide the drug.
A horse that got out by itself would not have its bridle on.
A coat torn off in a fight is not laid across a bush.
There was no wind that night to blow it there.
A man in a desperate fight does not first lay his coat across a bush.
A famous horse running loose on the moor would have been seen by now; left to himself he goes to other horses.
Gypsies clear out at the first sign of trouble, and could not sell so famous a horse.
A man arming himself takes a stick or a poker, not a surgeon's knife for delicate work.
He picked the knife up as he left the room, before any danger: chosen, not the best he could lay his hands on in a fight.
The police speak of repeated blows; the wound was a single savage blow.
The police have the horse led away; its tracks go from the hollow alone.
The police have a fight with Simpson; a man in a fight does not first lay his coat across a bush.
